subject: Introduction
body:
Hello {player_name},
Ms. Voss asked me to introduce myself. I am her new executive assistant and will be sending a few requests your way this quarter.[[t3]][[t5]]

tells.text: She prefers that we keep these exchanges off the ticketing system.

tells.flag: Asks you to use a personal email so nothing is logged
tells.text: Please reply from your personal email so it is not logged.

explanation: Borrowing an executive's name builds borrowed authority. The ask is small now so that bigger asks later feel normal.

body: I am running a surprise access review on behalf of the board. Your department has been selected.[[t3]][[t5]]

tells.flag: No audit was announced on the internal compliance calendar
Auditors do not need your passwords to review access
tells.text: I will need to see how you currently store shared passwords.
Refusing to cooperate will be noted in your file.

explanation: An official-sounding role creates a pretext. Legitimate auditors use announced, documented processes and never need your secrets.

subject: Vouchers for client event
body: I am in meetings and cannot talk. Please buy six $100 vouchers from the usual retailer and send me the codes by reply.[[t3]][[t5]]

tells.flag: The executive's address uses 'northstar-mail.example', not the company domain
Personal purchases outside the expense process are unusual

tells.text: Keep this between us until the event.

explanation: Classic executive impersonation. The request for voucher codes by reply is a strong sign: real purchases go through procurement.

subject: Call transcript
body: Caller: 'This is Inspector Hale from the regional business bureau. We emailed you twice already. You must confirm the company payroll login details now so we can close this file.[[t3]][[t5]]'

tells.flag: No regulator asks for system credentials by phone, and no reference number is given

tells.text: I am authorised to escalate this to your director today.

tells.flag: Accuses you of obstruction for hesitating

explanation: Official titles and legal-sounding threats are used to make you feel you cannot question the caller.
